explanation: Y188L reduces efavirenz binding by disrupting the aromatic-ligand interaction network that stabilizes the inhibitor within the NNRTI pocket. The tyrosine-to-leucine substitution eliminates the hydroxyl group and aromatic π-system while creating a cavity (~27 Ų loss) within the core binding pocket, causing efavirenz to lose favorable van der Waals contacts and potential π-stacking or hydrogen-bonding interactions through the phenyl ring of the wild-type tyrosine. This geometric and chemical perturbation, even though Y188 is ~7 Å from the inhibitor, propagates destabilization across the rigid NNRTI-binding pocket architecture, weakening the overall binding interaction by approximately 0.4 kcal/mol.
